sections.title: Getting started
sections.summary: Plug in the controller, copy the Remote Scripts folder into your Live User Library, start Live. The script starts the Maschine Bridge, which takes over the hardware: no Controller Editor, no MIDI mode, a real SHIFT key. Your note repeat rate, arp settings, chord type and voicing, drum colours and velocity curve are remembered between Live sessions.

sections.title: KEYBOARD: notes in key
sections.summary: The pads walk up Live's current scale (root note bright). Root and scale are Live's own, so changing them here changes Live's Scale settings and vice versa, including per-clip scales.

sections.title: CHORDS: chord sets
sections.summary: Every pad plays a chord built from Live's scale, starting on successive scale degrees, so every chord is in key.

sections.title: STEP: step sequencer
sections.summary: The pads are 16 steps of the focused sound (the focused drum pad, or the last keyboard note) in the focused clip. The playhead runs across the pads while the clip plays.

sections.title: Playing: velocity, repeat, arp, touch strip
sections.summary: The bridge plays the notes itself, next to the hardware, so the pads can do things one-note-per-pad MIDI can't: chords, arpeggios, note repeat that follows pressure, 16 velocities.

sections.title: PLUG-IN: device parameters (MIKRO)
sections.summary: The encoder controls one parameter of the selected device at a time. Parameters come in pages: Ableton's own banks for Live's devices (Filter, Envelope...), the visible macros of a rack, or groups of 8 for plug-ins. The screen shows the device, the page, and the parameter's name and value. Each device remembers where you were.
